text: In Crispin Wright's pluralism about truth, the property a statement has when it is assertible on some state of information and would remain assertible no matter how that information were improved or enlarged is called ___.
explanation: Wright introduces superassertibility as a truth property that is available in every domain but may be the only truth property in areas such as ethics, where there are arguably no mind-independent facts beyond ideal warranted assertibility. In domains with mind-independent facts, such as physics, truth may additionally be correspondence — which is why, for Wright, realism debates turn on which richer property a domain supports.
